articles.title: Johnny Depp’s ‘Ebenezer’ Comeback: A Smaller $5 Million Salary, Optimistic Theater Owners and More
articles.summary: Four years ago, Johnny Depp’s fans and detractors descended on the sleepy town of Fairfax, Virginia, to cheer or jeer the actor in his ugly defamation case a...
articles.body:
Four years ago, Johnny Depp's fans and detractors descended on the sleepy town of Fairfax, Virginia, to cheer or jeer the actor in his ugly defamation case against ex-wife Amber Heard. Now, when local cinema operator Mark O'Meara probes his patrons about "Ebenezer," a new take on "A Christmas Carol" featuring Depp as the coldhearted miser Scrooge, he's met with decidedly less intensity about the embattled star's first major movie role in nearly eight years.

"Some people can't wait. They love Johnny Depp. And others are just like, 'Meh,'" says O'Meara, who owns Fairfax's University Mall and Cinema Arts theatres. "I don't think it's a polarizing thing."

"Ebenezer" isn't expected to ignite the box office à la "Michael," a musical biopic about a controversial figure. The Dickens adaptation, which opens on Nov. 13, is tracking a modest debut of about $20 million domestically and another $20 million overseas from 63 markets. But O'Meara doesn't get the sense the public sees Depp as persona non grata, even though the actor's career has been derailed by personal drama, including domestic abuse allegations leveled by Heard.

Paramount, meanwhile, is betting that moviegoers have been missing Depp, whose last Hollywood outing was 2018's "Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald." (He was forced by Warner Bros. to exit the "Harry Potter" spinoff series in 2020 after losing a libel case against the British tabloid The Sun, which called the actor a "wife beater." Depp won the subsequent defamation trial in the U.S.) An April 2026 study by the National Research Group suggests his fans never turned on him. Participants ranked Depp among the top 10 actors — ahead of Tom Hanks and behind Margot Robbie — who "would make you most interested in seeing a new movie in a cinema in the future."

"Audiences don't care. He's still one of the biggest movie stars on the planet," says Kevin Goetz, founder and CEO of audience research firm Screen Engine/ASI. "That, to me, is very telling about how often Hollywood perpetuates its own self-fulfilling prophecies."

As Hollywood has kept a distance, Depp has remained a popular figure around the world, receiving career achievement and tribute awards from international film festivals and retaining a $20 million brand deal with Dior. Onscreen, he has appeared in underseen indies like the 2020 drama "Minamata" and the 2023 period piece "Jeanne du Barry," and he directed the 2024 biopic "Modì, Three Days on the Wing of Madness." And Depp's fans have been vocal on social media, supporting the actor through his professional struggles and bizarrely rallying in 2021 to nominate "Minamata" for the Oscars first (and only) fan favorite award.

Lately, the town seems willing to forgive Depp. His next film is Lionsgate's 2027 action thriller "Day Drinker," co-starring Penélope Cruz. Meanwhile Disney is looking into "Ebenezer" and the potential backlash, before greenlighting another "Pirates of the Caribbean" movie, according to sources. Depp has said he's open to returning to the franchise , but he noted "the only involvement I really want to have, truly, is just to send them off on a better note."

"Ebenezer" doesn't need to electrify the masses to justify its price tag. Given the uncertainty, Paramount cautiously spent $38 million to produce the Dickens tale. Depp was paid $5 million, a fraction of what he's earned on prior studio movies, with the promise of bonuses tied to box office performance. Marketing expenses were around $50 million, including stops at San Diego Comic- Con where the actor made a surprise appearance, dressed in character, and threw handfuls of candy at the foot of attendees. (Paramount declined to comment on budgets.) Directed by Ti West, known for the "X" horror trilogy, "Ebenezer" spins the oft-told yarn of the curmudgeonly businessman who is visited by the ghosts of Christmas past, present and future.

"I'm optimistic for a few reasons," says Regal's CEO Eduardo Acuna. "Even though this story predates him, it feels like the character was written for Johnny Depp. And it's good IP from a very distinctive filmmaker."

Cinema operators like Acuna suggest the box office haul will speak less to Depp's appeal and more to the movie's quality. After all, there's been no shortage of takes on "A Christmas Carol." Scrooge has been a staple of holiday moviegoing for decades, with popular versions including the 1951 classic with Alastair Sim and 1988's "Scrooged" with Bill Murray. The most recent entry, Disney's 2009 "A Christmas Carol," starring Jim Carrey, brought in $325 million against an overinflated $200 million budget.

"It's a story that's been told a number of times, so it'll be more about whether this one is compelling," says Classic Cinemas CEO Chris Johnson. "I don't know if I've heard anyone saying they won't see it because of Johnny Depp. The public seems to be pretty forgiving."

For Depp, embodying a misanthrope like Scrooge — in the trailer, he's seen scaring villagers and being stingy with Christmas bonuses — jibes with the other offbeat or unlikable characters he's spun into the stuff of contemporary cinema classics. His real-life rebellious persona has helped sell his most famous roles, from the chaotic Captain Jack Sparrow from "Pirates of the Caribbean," eccentric Willy Wonka from "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory" and the mercurial Mad Hatter in "Alice in Wonderland."

"Johnny's image was built on being a bad boy," Goetz says. "He ain't America's dad. We don't want him to be that."

articles.title: Céline Dion head bangs with Jack Black at Metallica concert in the Sphere
articles.summary: Who knew Céline Dion was a secret metalhead?
articles.body: Who knew Céline Dion was a secret metalhead? The 58-year-old singer and her 16-year-old twin sons, Eddy and Nelson, rocked out alongside actor Jack Black at Metallica’s concert at Sphere in Las Vegas on Nov. 7. A fan video that went viral showed Dion dancing and playing air guitar as the legendary heavy metal band performed on stage. Just a few feet away, Black vigorously nodded his head and pointed his fingers in the air in time with the music. Wes Zirkle, who shot the video, attended the concert with his college best friend Ben to celebrate their 51st birthdays. The pair weren’t too shocked to see Black thrashing in the stands, but Dion? “I was really surprised to see Céline Dion like really, really into this concert,” Zirkle tells TODAY.com. The fan reaction to his video showing the unlikely duo sharing a love of Metallica has been “a lot of fun,” Zirkle adds. One fan commented, “I was so focused on Jack Black I totally almost missed Celine Dion. A sentence I never thought I’d say.” “The next duet we need,” another joked. Dion, whose public outings were limited in recent years after she was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome diagnosis, is on temporary break from her triumphant record-breaking comeback Paris residency. The concerts resume in May 2027. Dion shared images from the Metallica show, which showed her posing with Metallica members James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Rob Trujillo. “Thank you James, Lars, Kirk and Robert and everyone from the @Metallica organization for the warm welcome! We had such a wonderful time seeing you at the Sphere. We absolutely loved the show,” she wrote, adding a devil horn hand gesture emoji. Metallica responded in the comments by posting three black hearts. Dion also shared a cute pic of her and her sons posing with Black at the concert. The multi-Grammy winner revealed her love for Metallica in February when she named a few musical acts on her most current playlist in an Instagram video. After the “My Heart Will Go On” singer shared that Metallica was her son Eddy’s “favorite” band, she did a hilarious imitation of Hetfield scream-singing his ferocious lyrics. Metallica’s initial series of dates for its “Life Burns Faster” residency at Sphere ran from Oct. 1 through Nov. 7. The band’s residency resumes in January 2027 and wraps in March 2027.

articles.title: Broncano hace autocrítica tras su entrevista a Santiago Abascal en La Revuelta: "Me arrepiento de muchas cosas"
articles.standfirst: El presentador ha respondido a todas las preguntas en las inmediaciones del Teatro Albéniz
articles.summary: El presentador ha respondido a todas las preguntas en las inmediaciones del Teatro Albéniz
articles.body: David Broncano ha admitido que se equivocó en el formato de entrevista que le planteó a Santiago Abascal. El presentador de 'La Revuelta' ha sido claro con lo sucedido el pasado lunes 9 de noviembre en el Teatro Albéniz durante la grabación de la entrevista con motivo de las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. De hecho, en la entrada a la grabación del martes 10 con Ada Colau, admitió de entrada que no estaba bien con el resultado final: "Estoy triste porque creo que no lo hice bien. No lo hice bien ayer". "Creo que me equivoqué con varias cosas, con cómo se hizo y demás. Y pues estoy triste porque no me gusta...", siguió diciendo antes de que se acercaran más medios allí presentes. De hecho, hizo autocrítica ya que admite que igual no tendría que haber renunciado a muchas cosas, entre ellas el humor: "Me arrepiento de muchas cosas, posiblemente tenía que haber utilizado la comedia más, como hago siempre, pero era complicado. También sé que había mucha gente que me decía que con políticos no hagamos bromas." Al ser preguntado por la imagen que dio Santiago Abascal en el programa, se sinceró separando su opinión política con lo transmitido por el entrevistado: "Abascal lo hizo bien, la verdad. Ellos, tanto él como como la gente de comunicación del partido, (...) lo digo a nivel estratégico, creo que lo han hecho bien porque ellos nos pidieron venir con su público, con gente elegida por Vox". "Esa es la clave de todo", señala el cómico sobre la importancia del público en el desarrollo de la entrevista. Una reflexión que continuó: "Para mí es la clave de cómo salió la entrevista porque nosotros aceptamos hacerlo con público seleccionado por Vox porque yo pensaba, evidentemente fui demasiado ambicioso, posiblemente vanidoso y me extralimité en mis capacidades, pensaba que eso podía evitar que luego ellos si no salía la entrevista como querían o que no... con nuestro público les podía llevar a excusarse en eso, que no les hemos dejado hablar, que el público les ha silvado, que les ha abucheado y demás" Una reflexión que finaliza: "Yo pensé que quería quitarles esa cosa, que sé que a veces lo hacen desde Vox y pues me equivoqué, porque en la práctica cuando empezó la entrevista vi, todos lo visteis, que era muy desigual y era muy injusto. Para el público también es por qué le están aplaudiendo cada cosa". De hecho, reconoce que no le gustó cómo estuvo: "Estuve incómodo conmigo mismo, cuando me di cuenta que había generado un ambiente raro y que había generado una situación que creo que no merece una entrevista a un responsable político, en cuanto a que esté tan sesgada de cara a la reacción del público y demás". Y hace autocrítica: "Yo mismo me tiré toda la entrevista diciendo 'me he equivocado, he pensado que era buena idea pero la he cagado'. (...) Veía muchas veces que Santiago estaba hablando y yo estaba pensando por dentro: 'Tío, eres tonto, lo has hecho mal, esto no tiene sentido'. Entonces, tampoco me permitía responderle con la velocidad que habría que haberlo hecho". Un análisis que continuó dando pinceladas con cómo vió al líder de Vox en el programa: "Igual que dije que Abascal estratégicamente lo hizo bien ayer y comunicativamente también, tuvo mucho plomo, digamos que muchas de las cosas que dijo cuando las analizas despacio son muy cuestionables, pero lo hizo bien técnicamente. Formalmente, digamos". Y ante alusiones, lo comparaba con el presidente del Gobierno: "Con Sánchez pasó un poco parecido. Ayer con Abascal, hay muchas cosas en las que todo el mundo sabe que tenemos grandes diferencias, pero creo que lo llevé a un camino... una vez que pasó lo del público, me di cuenta, lo llevé a un camino excesivo porque le quité toda la comedia y toda la distensión de algunas cosas que creo que habría estado bien". Además, son muchas las críticas que ha recibido el presentador de La Revuelta por las entrevistas a los políticos y reconoce: "Yo no he querido hacer ninguna de estas entrevistas. Entiendo que haya muchos periodistas y muchas periodistas que no les haga especial gracia, que haga yo una entrevista así, pero no es una decisión mía, no he peleado yo por entrevistar a los políticos". Justo antes de admitir que no lo hizo bien: "Esto es un muy buen marrón que me ha caído al estar en televisión pública en el programa con más espectadores de la cadena y que ha sucedido así, que yo intentaba hacer con responsabilidad. Intentar hacer el servicio público que se supone que hay que hacer en la cadena, en La 1 y desde luego ayer no fue el caso".

articles.title: Ableton Live 13 announced with a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more
articles.summary: Live 13 is one of the biggest updates to Ableton’s music-making suite in years, adding a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more.
articles.body: Today, Ableton announced Live 13, which is expected to arrive in early 2027 with a slew of new features. Most of the changes are seemingly minor on paper, but when combined, they make for the biggest update to the digital audio workstation (DAW) in years. The feature most likely to draw attention is the addition of a proper step sequencer. While Ableton’s Push controller had a dedicated step sequencer, and you could effectively use the piano roll as one, the desktop app never included one. Ableton didn’t phone this feature in either — it’s a powerful sequencer. You can change velocity, timing, chance, length, and repeats for each step in the grid. Each track can have its own length, playback rate, and direction, letting you create something complex and evolving. [Media: The addition of ARA plugin support will also likely excite pro producers and vocalists. This means compatible plugins can now be used directly on audio in the DAW. For example, pitch correction and time-stretching tool Melodyne previously required you to import audio from Ableton into Melodyne, then render it back out to a track in your DAW. Now it can clean up messy vocal takes directly in Live’s UI. Ableton has also added a new mixer view that lets you see all the loaded devices on a track in a compact vertical view. Here you can drag and drop them between tracks, or copy and paste them. It also makes it much easier to navigate a sprawling 30-track session quickly at a glance. My personal favorite new addition is Looplet, an experimental looping instrument with four playheads and a ton of options for manipulating your audio. It offers granular processing, filtering, pitch and speed control, and each playhead can be routed to individual tracks for additional processing. It’s a powerful tool for ambient and soundtrack work. The full list of new features is sprawling, so here are just a few more highlights: * A new drum synth with more than 20 different models across nine categories spanning classic drum machines and experimental abstract percussion. * Capture now includes not just MIDI notes but automation as well. * Contextual browsing lets you swap instruments and presets directly in the device view, reducing the need to open the main browser. * Multiband racks for processing different frequencies through different effect chains. * A bread-and-butter transient shaper for tightening up drum sounds. * Envelope clips on return tracks for automating effects. * Racks can now have up to 32 macros and custom mapping curves. * Custom layouts on Push 3 for combining mixers, note grids, step sequencers, and more.

articles.title: Todd Chrisley, 57, Says He’s ‘Not Condoning’ Daughter Savannah, 29, Marrying ‘Someone That’s My Age’
articles.summary: Todd Chrisley is opening up about his concerns over daughter Savannah Chrisley‘s marriage to a man nearly twice her age. The Chrisley Knows Best star, 57, di...
articles.body:
Todd Chrisley is opening up about his concerns over daughter Savannah Chrisley 's marriage to a man nearly twice her age.

The Chrisley Knows Best star, 57, discussed his feelings about Savannah's husband, Jason Galanis , during a conversation shared on the Instagram account for her Unlocked with Savannah Chrisley podcast, on Monday, November 9.

"Jason is not who I would have chosen for my daughter," Todd admitted.

"Well, no, because there's a massive age gap…" Savannah, 29, replied.

Galanis, 56, a businessman with a background in finance, is 27 years older than his wife.

In the Instagram video, Todd recalled how he reacted when his daughter first told him about the relationship.

"I said, 'Let me stop you … don't tell me anything because I am not interested in hearing it. If that is what you have chosen to do with your life, you need to keep it separate from my life because I am not condoning my daughter marrying someone or being tied up with someone that's my age.' And I saw the hurt," he said.

However, Todd explained that his feelings changed after watching how Galanis treated Savannah.

"So my thing is that I want you to be happy, but most importantly I want you to be whole, and a man never makes you whole," he said during the chat.

Fans had mixed reactions in the Instagram comment section.

"Todd is being honest. He wouldn't have picked Jason but his daughter's happiness comes first," one person wrote.

Another defended Savannah's decision, commenting, "She's a grown adult, she needs to make her own choices without judgement! She did it, let her live her life!"

As In Touch previously reported , Savannah and Galanis are expecting their first child together, a baby boy.

The couple secretly married in the Cayman Islands on July 14, People reported.

articles.title: Carlos Alsina también se pronuncia sobre la entrevista de Abascal en ‘La Revuelta’ y desvela el “error fundamental del planteamiento”
articles.standfirst: El periodista ha hablado de ello en ‘Al rojo vivo’, de La Sexta
articles.summary: El periodista ha hablado de ello en ‘Al rojo vivo’, de La Sexta
articles.body: Este martes, 10 de noviembre, el tema del día ha sido, sin duda, la entrevista de Santiago Abascal en ‘La Revuelta’, espacio presentado por David Broncano. De esta forma, todavía se siguen produciendo reacciones al respecto. Una de las últimas ha sido la de Carlos Alsina, quien ha señalado “el error fundamental del planteamiento” que hizo que el formato se alejara de lo que habitualmente es. “Empiezo por lo que me pareció inaceptable del programa de anoche, que es que en la televisión pública de mi país se acepte la exigencia o petición o condición que pone un líder político para ir a un programa, que es que el público de ese programa lo pone el partido político a cuyo líder se va a entrevistar”, comenzaba diciendo el periodista en ‘Al rojo vivo’, de La Sexta. “Yo creo que hay condiciones o exigencias que no se deben aceptar, ni en un programa de una productora privada, ni en un programa de Televisión Española, ni en ningún programa bajo mi punto de vista, pero especialmente en la televisión pública”, detalló. “Creo que el propio David Broncano se dio cuenta de ello a medida que avanzaba el programa”, proseguía, dejando claro que el asunto del público fue lo más grave. El presentador en Onda Cero apuntó que, “si tienes a un público que te ha traído el partido a cuyo líder estás entrevistando, aquello se convierte en una ovación permanente a cualquier cosa que diga el entrevistado”. Por lo que “efectivamente complica mucho la conversación, entrevista o como lo queráis llamar”. Además, Alsina rompía una lanza a favor de Broncano, detallando que “no es un periodista y por tanto no le debemos juzgar”. “Yo creo que él hace algo que a mí me parece que es muy honrado, que es sabiendo que viene alguien a un programa que es un programa que está claramente en contra de esa posición política, de ese invitado, es plantearle a ese invitado todo lo que se dice de él cuando no está”. Finalmente, el comunicador confesaba una alternativa que se podría haber hecho: “Hacer el programa sin público, se habría evitado los abucheos, las ovaciones y todo aquello que aparentemente iba a distorsionar la conversación”.

articles.title: El Consejo de Informativos de TVE cuestiona la entrevista de David Broncano a Santiago Abascal y pide asumir responsabilidades
articles.standfirst: Considera que 'La Revuelta' incurrió en "errores graves" al convertir un espacio de entretenimiento en un programa político sin el rigor exigible
articles.summary: Considera que 'La Revuelta' incurrió en "errores graves" al convertir un espacio de entretenimiento en un programa político sin el rigor exigible
articles.body: El Consejo de Informativos de Televisión Española (TVE) ha reclamado que se asuman responsabilidades por la entrevista que David Broncano realizó este lunes al líder de Vox, Santiago Abascal, en 'La Revuelta'. En un comunicado, el órgano ha calificado de "errores graves" tanto el cambio de público habitual como el abandono de la esencia del programa, basada en el humor y el entretenimiento, y ha reconocido que la emisión les hizo sentirse "muy incómodos". "La Revuelta' de anoche nos hizo sentir muy incómodos", comienza el comunicado del Consejo de Informativos de la televisión pública, que considera que el espacio de David Broncano se convirtió en un programa informativo, pero sin el rigor que debería garantizar un espacio de estas características. A su juicio, alguien dentro de RTVE permitió que la entrevista al líder de Vox se presentara como una conversación "seria" sin que se cumplieran las condiciones profesionales que exige el tratamiento informativo de una entrevista política. La intervención de Santiago Abascal provocó un cambio evidente en el tono habitual del programa. El líder de Vox aprovechó su presencia en el espacio para desplegar algunos de los principales argumentos de su discurso político, con ataques al presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, al que volvió a calificar de "dictador", además de negar la violencia machista y el cambio climático y calificar la situación migratoria de Ceuta de "invasión". Por su parte, David Broncano se mostró incómodo ante algunas de las declaraciones del dirigente político y este martes ha reconocido públicamente que se equivocó al abordar la entrevista a Santiago Abascal. El Consejo de Informativos aclara que su comunicado no pretende analizar "si se debería haber hecho y cómo se hizo" la entrevista, pero sí considera que una entrevista política, especialmente durante un proceso electoral, debe realizarse desde los servicios informativos y por profesionales de la información de RTVE. Además, el órgano defiende que este tipo de contenidos debe contar con producción "100% interna", algo que, según denuncia, no sucedió en esta ocasión. "Alguien de RTVE permitió que esta entrevista se presentara como 'seria", señala el comunicado, que concluye con una petición expresa de responsabilidades: "Por eso creemos que alguien debería asumir las responsabilidades". La reacción del Consejo de Informativos añade así presión sobre la dirección de RTVE después de una entrevista que ha generado controversia tanto por el contenido de las declaraciones de Santiago Abascal como por el formato elegido para abordar una conversación política en un programa concebido para el entretenimiento.

articles.title: We read Sofia Franklyn’s memoir about her falling out with Alex Cooper so you don’t have to
articles.summary: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.”
articles.body: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.” Sofia Franklyn, who co-created the famous podcast with Alex Cooper, released her memoir “Daddy Issues” on Tuesday, in which she details her falling out with her now ex-friend. The duo shot to viral fame in 2018, when the podcast was still under Barstool Sports. It became known for candid conversations about commonly taboo topics for women to discuss publicly, including raunchy sex stories. But the two professionally split up in 2020, news that initially shocked their listeners. Cooper went on to host the podcast solo, eventually moving it to Spotify and now SiriusXM in lucrative deals that helped propel her to mainstream success. Meanwhile, Franklyn, who is an influencer with over 619,000 Instagram followers, launched her own podcast titled “Sofia with an F.” Over the years, rumors had circulated about what exactly happened between Franklyn and Cooper. Here are some of the biggest claims in Franklyn’s 240-page book. Warnings from others in Cooper’s orbit Growing up in Utah with a single mom, Franklyn writes about struggling to find a clear path. She was arrested three times: once for using a fake ID and twice for underage drinking. Eventually, she left to start anew in New York City, largely to escape an abusive relationship. But her early days in the city were far from ideal. She lived with her aunt and was working at Morgan Stanley in a job under a toxic boss who she claims harassed her regularly. She eventually moved into her own place that she could barely afford and found herself feeling extremely lonely. Until she met Cooper. A random girl Franklyn befriended in a ride share connected her to Cooper and her childhood friend, Lauren, who were looking for a third roommate. Cooper and Franklyn ended up becoming inseparable, with Lauren largely out of the picture as she spent much of her time with her boyfriend. But one night, Franklyn writes, Lauren and her shared a rare evening in the apartment alone together. That’s when Lauren asked Franklyn whether she thought it was weird that Cooper “tossed” her aside. “You showed up and it was like I never existed,” Franklyn said Lauren told her, which prompted Franklyn to apologize. Lauren also told Franklyn that Cooper “uses you because you’re hot, to like, go to parties and stuff.” At the time, Franklyn wrote that she felt defensive of her friendship with Cooper and did not think of it as “using” her. But later, another close friend of Cooper’s from childhood also seemingly warned her that Cooper was not going to stick with her. Muji, known to early “Call Her Daddy” listeners as “Milfhunter,” worked on the podcast with the duo. He told Franklyn that Cooper “doesn’t have friends. I’ve watched it happen since high school.” When Cooper abruptly fired Muji, Franklyn said he told her: “She’s gonna f--- you.” An alleged firing attempt, secret raise and IP disagreement Cooper and Frankyn’s stars rose quickly at Barstool, as the two took creative control of their show with company founder Dave Portnoy’s blessing. But Franklyn started to feel things change after the Barstool holiday party. That night, she felt “insane anxiety,” drank excessively and fought with Cooper. An angry Cooper told Franklyn she was “rude” and “aggressive” toward her at the party and that everyone, including Portnoy, had noticed and wanted to fire her. Franklyn says she wanted to apologize to Portnoy for her behavior, but was told not to by Cooper. When she finally did say something, Portnoy appeared to dismiss it, saying “the girls got in a fight.” It wasn’t until later, Franklyn writes, that she learned Cooper used the party as a way to negotiate a raise for herself. Muji purportedly told her that Cooper said, “If I have to put up with her, I need more money.” She got the raise: $20,000 more than Franklyn every year. “She didn’t tell you because she didn’t want you to know she tried to get you fired,” Franklyn said Muji told her. In 2020, when the duo was negotiating their new contract together, Franklyn wrote they sent Barstool an email with a new proposal in which they asked for “50/50 split of all revenue derived from Barstool’s exploitation of the property (i.e., advertisers, sponsors, merch, etc.)” and a “minimum guarantee — $1M each, per year.” The negotiations centered around the IP for “Call Her Daddy,” which Barstool Sports owned and could technically continue without Franklyn or Cooper attached. Amid their talks with Barstool, Franklyn said she and Cooper agreed their goal was staying together. They even came up with a spin-off podcast if the negotiations fell through, titling it “The Fathers.” “We’re being corny as s---, but it’s because we’re both blissed out on the plan and our future — we don’t know how Barstool will respond, but we know that staying together is more important than losing the IP, or whatever they may threaten. What is the name without us?” But in the end, Franklyn was ousted as co-host. Portnoy called Franklyn to tell her that Cooper had met with him separately and proposed going on without Franklyn. “She came to me with a plan, and I needed an episode. There’s no clear favorite,” he told her, according to Franklyn’s memoir. “You could always have your own show, and we promote the shit out of it like we did with Call Her Daddy. I think it would be huge.” Portnoy also said Cooper had hired her own lawyer and claimed that Franklyn had been “the one that’s been dragging this on, and she’s been ready to sign this thing.” Franklyn claims Cooper subsequently locked her out of their shared social accounts and posted a 52-minute YouTube break-up video called “The Truth about Call Her Daddy” in which she described Franklyn as a “liability.” Six years later, the video is still up and has amassed 4.6 million views. Representatives for Portnoy and Cooper did not respond to requests for comment on Tuesday. Cooper’s alleged legal threat The book opens with a scene in which Franklyn’s book agent calls her to say she received an angry call from Matt Kaplan. Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in 2024. The couple co-founded the Unwell Network, a subsidiary of the media company Trending. Franklyn writes that her agent told her Kaplan said Cooper would sue. Representatives from Unwell told the New York Times that Kaplan “never discussed the book’s claims or any intent to sue the author with Verve.” A representative for Kaplan did not respond to a request for comment on Tuesday. Verve, Franklyn’s literary agency, also did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.title: David Broncano pide perdón en 'La Revuelta' tras su entrevista a Santiago Abascal: "Me siento muy decepcionado conmigo mismo"
articles.standfirst: El presentador ha hecho autocrítica tras la polémica entrevista al líder de Vox, ha reconocido que no estuvo a la altura y ha pedido disculpas a los espectadores habituales del programa
articles.summary: El presentador ha hecho autocrítica tras la polémica entrevista al líder de Vox, ha reconocido que no estuvo a la altura y ha pedido disculpas a los espectadores habituales del programa
articles.body: David Broncano ha roto su silencio en 'La Revuelta' después de la polémica entrevista a Santiago Abascal, líder de Vox, emitida este lunes. El presentador ha aprovechado el inicio del programa de este martes para hacer autocrítica, reconocer los errores que cometió durante la conversación y pedir disculpas tanto a los espectadores como al público habitual del espacio de TVE, que no pudo acudir a la grabación debido a la presencia de los seguidores de Vox. "Me siento muy decepcionado conmigo mismo", ha admitido David Broncano, que ya había adelantado su malestar unas horas antes ante los periodistas que le esperaban a la salida del Teatro Albéniz. "Estoy triste, creo que no lo hice bien. Me equivoqué con varias cosas. Me arrepiento de muchas cosas", ha confesado el humorista, que considera que debería haber mantenido el tono humorístico que caracteriza al programa. El conductor de 'La Revuelta' ha explicado que durante la entrevista fue consciente de que no estaba actuando como suele hacerlo. "Me tiré toda la entrevista diciendo: 'La he cagado, me he equivocado, he pensado que era buena idea, pero la he cagado'. Vi muchas veces que Santiago estaba hablando y yo estaba pensando por dentro: 'Tío, eres tonto, lo has hecho mal, esto no tiene sentido", ha relatado. El presentador también ha reconocido que la decisión de entrevistar a los candidatos políticos no partió de él, sino que fue una responsabilidad que tuvo que asumir por estar al frente del programa con más espectadores de la cadena pública. "Era un muy buen marrón que me ha caído al estar en la televisión pública", ha manifestado David Broncano. El arranque de la emisión de este martes ha reflejado el cambio de tono respecto a la entrega anterior. Broncano ha entrado en el teatro en silencio, sin los habituales aplausos, vítores y música, mientras el público participaba en una escenificación en la que le lanzaba rollos de papel higiénico y otros objetos. "Soy la persona que más ha decepcionado a la izquierda después de Gabriel Rufián", ha bromeado inicialmente el presentador, antes de adoptar un tono más serio para dirigirse a los espectadores. Una de sus principales disculpas ha estado dedicada a los seguidores habituales del programa, que no pudieron acudir a la grabación del lunes. "Quiero disculparme con el público que no pudo venir ayer al programa, que es nuestro público de verdad. Me disculpo en nombre de todos ellos", ha afirmado. "Es uno de los momentos más tristes de mi vida reciente. Me siento mal por haber decepcionado a tanta gente. Soy consciente de que hay personas que esperan más del programa y ayer no estuve a la altura", ha añadido. En lugar de seguir la dinámica habitual de preguntar a varios asistentes del público, David Broncano ha dado la vuelta al formato y ha permitido que fueran ellos quienes le plantearan preguntas y compartieran sus impresiones sobre la entrevista a Santiago Abascal. Entre las críticas que han surgido durante la conversación, varios espectadores han coincidido en señalar como uno de los principales errores que Vox pudiera elegir al público asistente y que la entrevista se desarrollara con un tono tan alejado del habitual en 'La Revuelta'. El programa también ha recurrido al humor para rebajar la tensión. Grison ha intervenido con una de sus habituales bromas: "Al menos sabemos que si esta gente entra a gobernar nos tiran. Bueno, después de lo de anoche, si sigue el PSOE igual también". Con estas explicaciones, David Broncano ha querido dar la cara tras una entrevista que ha generado un intenso debate y numerosas reacciones en las redes sociales, donde, pese al apoyo recibido por parte de muchos espectadores, también ha sido objeto de críticas.

articles.title: El público habitual de 'La Revuelta' reprende a David Broncano tras la entrevista a Santiago Abascal: "Si a nadie se le ha permitido que ponga su público, a él tampoco"
articles.standfirst: El presentador ha pedido a los asistentes que expusieran sus apreciaciones
articles.summary: El presentador ha pedido a los asistentes que expusieran sus apreciaciones
articles.body: Este martes, 10 de noviembre, ‘La Revuelta’ ha vuelto un día más en la franja horaria del ‘access prime time’ de La 1 de RTVE. Sin embargo, esta ocasión, como podía ser otra forma, ha arrancado con David Broncano haciendo mención al tema del día: su entrevista a Santiago Abascal en el Teatro Albéniz de Madrid. “Quiero disculparme con el público que no pudo venir ayer al programa, que es nuestro público de verdad. Evidentemente, cometimos un error. Me disculpo ante vosotros en nombre de ellos y de toda la gente que viene al programa cada día. Me siento muy decepcionado conmigo por las decisiones que tomé de cara a la entrevista de ayer y cómo la lleve a cabo también. Hacía tiempo que no estaba tan triste con nada en mi vida”, expresaba Broncano. Dicho esto, el comunicador jienense ha dado paso a los asistentes que han acudido para que expusieran sus apreciaciones y sus quejas sobre la charla con el líder de VOX. “Lo estuve viendo ayer y me pareció que el mayor fallo fue cambiar el planteamiento de la entrevista. Tenía que haber ido por el cauce normal porque le diste un poco de ventaja. Fue casi una entrevista política y quien es profesional en eso tiene ventaja”, decía un hombre. “Pensé lo mismo según estaba sucediendo la cosa. Es verdad que es más fácil decirlo ahora al acabar. Sé que mucha gente dice ‘no estés a cachondeo con él’ e intenté hacerla un tono periodístico”, contestaba el presentador. Por otro lado, otra mujer le decía lo siguiente: “Tenías una situación muy complicada. Como público objetivo, si a nadie se le ha permitido que ponga su público a él tampoco”. “VOX no se quería exponer a que no les dejaran hablar y yo les dije que sí. La cagué tremenda. Mi idea era que si ellos venían con el público habitual les iba a servir para decir que no me han dejado hablar y que había censura. Lo que pasé es que infravaloraré la fuerza de 400 personas aplaudiendo cada frase que decía. Me afectó y a partir de ahí mi cabeza tenía todo el rato por encima ‘soy gilipollas, la he cagado’, tenía siete cosas en la cabeza”, sentenciaba Broncano.

articles.title: Ada Colau carga contra la entrevista a Santiago Abascal en 'La Revuelta': "Vino un 'señoro' de extrema derecha"
articles.standfirst: La candidata del Frente Amplio ha reprochado al programa de David Broncano haber dado protagonismo al líder de Vox y ha considerado que sus declaraciones no podían quedar sin respuesta
articles.summary: La candidata del Frente Amplio ha reprochado al programa de David Broncano haber dado protagonismo al líder de Vox y ha considerado que sus declaraciones no podían quedar sin respuesta
articles.body: Ada Colau ha visitado este martes 'La Revuelta', un día después de la entrevista de David Broncano a Santiago Abascal. La candidata del Frente Amplio a las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre no ha querido pasar por alto la presencia del líder de Vox en el programa de La 1 y ha expresado abiertamente su malestar por el contenido y las circunstancias que rodearon su intervención. "Ayer vino un 'señoro' de extrema derecha que dijo muchas opiniones que vulneran derechos humanos", ha afirmado la exalcaldesa de Barcelona nada más aparecer en el escenario. Ada Colau ha añadido que "Santiago Abascal ya fue suficientemente protagonista, y hoy no tiene que serlo más", en referencia a la repercusión que había tenido la visita del de Vox. Ada Colau también ha cuestionado algunas de las afirmaciones del dirigente de Vox, que ha calificado de "mentiras objetivas" y "bulos" que, a su juicio, no podían quedar sin respuesta. "Un poco nerviosa" y consciente de la "responsabilidad compartida" después de lo sucedido en el programa anterior, ha querido dejar claro desde el principio que no conocía al público presente y que se alegraba de que no fuera el mismo que había asistido a la entrevista de Santiago Abascal. La visita de Ada Colau llegaba después de una de las entrevistas más complicadas de la trayectoria de David Broncano en 'La Revuelta'. La intervención de Santiago Abascal estuvo marcada por las condiciones planteadas por el equipo de Vox para gestionar la asistencia de público, que provocaron que el público habitual del programa no pudiera acudir, así como por un tono alejado del humor que caracteriza al espacio de La 1. Ante la polémica, el presentador ha aprovechado los primeros minutos de la emisión para dirigirse a los espectadores y pedir disculpas por haber permitido que Vox condicionara la presencia del público y por considerar que él mismo "no había estado a la altura" de las circunstancias. Pese a sus críticas a la entrevista de Santiago Abascal, Ada Colau se ha mostrado "totalmente a favor" de que los políticos participen en espacios de entretenimiento y no exclusivamente en programas de carácter periodístico. La candidata defendió que la vida está formada por diferentes dimensiones y que la política no tiene por qué ocupar todos los espacios. "La política puede hacer tu vida mejor, pero bailar también, tener personas queridas y cuidarlas, reírte, todas son esenciales", ha reflexionado la líder de Frente Amplio. La entrevista de Ada Colau se enmarca en la ventana electoral que 'La Revuelta' ha abierto con motivo de los comicios generales del 29 de noviembre. Antes que ella habían pasado por el programa Pedro Sánchez (PSOE), Irene Montero (Podemos), Gabriel Rufián (ERC) y Santiago Abascal (Vox). Por el momento, solo queda pendiente la visita de Alberto Núñez Feijóo, candidato del Partido Popular.

articles.title: Quanto custa para promover uma música? Empresários respondem | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-baterista de Wesley Safadão revelou gasto de R$ 250 mil em divulgação. De influenciadores a perfis nas redes e playlists, ecossistema tem valores diferentes em cada gênero.
articles.summary: Ex-baterista de Wesley Safadão revelou gasto de R$ 250 mil em divulgação. De influenciadores a perfis nas redes e playlists, ecossistema tem valores diferentes em cada gênero.
articles.body:
Na última semana, o empresário Rod Bala disse ter gasto R$ 250 mil para promover a canção "Quero É Distância" , do cantor de forró Jotavê.

No vídeo publicado no seu perfil no Instagram, o executivo, que também é ex-baterista de Wesley Safadão, disse que o valor não incluía os custos com a produção musical e composição. Era só para fazer "a música andar".

Durante sua explicação, ele dividiu os valores da seguinte forma:

R$ 30 mil para divulgação em páginas nas redes sociais

R$ 100 mil em parceria com influenciadores

Em 13 dias, a canção soma mais de 1 milhão de visualizações no YouTube e 500 mil plays no Spotify. Rod Bala prometeu nas redes sociais dar mais detalhes sobre o resultado do investimento.

Ao justificar o gasto, o empresário contou, comparando o trabalho artístico a um outro qualquer :

"Por exemplo: se você abre uma loja de açaí, você vai dar [o produto] para alguém provar, o pessoal tem que saber que você abriu a loja. Se não, ninguém vai consumir. A música é igual, tem que chegar na galera."

Como o g1 já mostrou , a música que você ouve hoje e está em destaque nas paradas de sucesso do Brasil não cresceu, necessariamente, graças a um processo orgânico . Teve gasto com influenciador, dancinha e mais. Uma espécie de "jabá 2.0".

Porém, a novidade mostrada por Rod Bala trata da quantidade de dinheiro envolvida e de como o processo de divulgação musical se pulverizou, fazendo com que o dinheiro se torne um fator cada vez mais importante.

Cada espaço de divulgação oferece um retorno diferente.

No caso das playlists, empresários e artistas têm como foco o retorno de plays. No Spotify, principal plataforma de streaming no Brasil, usuários têm playlists públicas com mais de um milhão de salvamentos (número de pessoas que acompanham as atualizações constantes da playlist).

Estar presente em uma espaço como esse ajuda a inflacionar o número de plays de uma música .

🚨 Mesmo sendo uma prática comum e recorrente, pagar para estar em uma playlist não é permitido pelo Spotify. “Caso uma pessoa ou empresa esteja vendendo a inclusão em uma playlist, isso é considerado manipulação de streaming e viola as diretrizes do Spotify relacionadas à divulgação de músicas”, diz a plataforma.

As páginas e influenciadores cumprem o papel de vender ao público das redes sociais a impressão que aquela música é boa e/ou está em alta.

Essas páginas ou influenciadores, que acumulam milhares (ou milhões) de seguidores, recebem ao promover músicas em seus perfis. E aí está outro problema: via de regra, essa prática não é sinalizada como publicidade e o público, que vê a mesma música em destaque em vários perfis de música ou nos stories de grandes influenciadores, nem sempre entende que aquele sucesso não é orgânico.

🚨O Guia de Marketing e Publicidade para Influenciadores, do Conar, é claro: todo conteúdo que promove uma marca, produto ou serviço (e que tem contrapartida ou pagamento) "deve ser claramente identificado como publicitário".

O g1 apurou que, com cerca de R$ 5 mil, já dá para movimentar microinfluenciadores e gerar um burburinho. Mas para tentar chegar ao Top 50, por exemplo, é preciso desembolsar por volta de R$ 20 mil.

O aplicativo Spotify — Foto: Pew Nguyen/Pexels

Pagar para levar sua música mais longe não é bem uma novidade. O jabá é uma instituição consolidada e transformou o rádio e a televisão.

Com a internet, as redes sociais e o streaming, a mudança veio na pulverização dos meios de divulgação e nos novos parâmetros de sucesso .

Na última década, o sertanejo passou a ser exemplo nesse novo modelo da indústria musical.

Gravações de DVDs multimilionários, investimento redobrado em rádios e playlists em plataformas de streaming, além de toda uma rede de páginas nas redes sociais e influenciadores segmentados, fizeram com que o gênero virasse referência e construísse todo um ecossistema de promoção de músicas.

O segundo a entender como essa roda gira e a criar seu próprio modelo foi o pagode. Mas com um ecossistema um pouco diferente.

Com projetos audiovisuais mais modestos, páginas e influenciadores menos badalados, o que o pagode ainda tenta entender é a engrenagem das plataformas de streaming. E, até por isso, o forte investimento nas rádios segue como um grande trunfo no segmento.

Em 2019, o Menos É Mais investiu “só” R$ 11 mil para fazer o projeto "Churrasquinho do Menos É Mais" , um DVD intimista com regravações de sucessos do pagode.

Sete anos depois, a ideia virou o catalisador do maior grupo do gênero no momento e, falando de retorno financeiro, teve seu valor multiplicado em muitas e muitas vezes. Desde então, a gravação de rodas de samba no mesmo estilo virou febre, mas nada atingiu o sucesso do grupo de Brasília.

Andriws Moraes, sócio da GH Music, responsável por cuidar da carreira de pagodeiros como Menos É Mais e Dilsinho, conta que os valores, pensando em projetos de álbum e DVD de grandes artistas, giram em torno de R$ 800 mil e R$ 1 milhão.

Mais do que o valor investido, o empresário acredita que o fundamental é ter um calendário de investimento, que tenha regularidade, e com uma ideia clara dos objetivos.

"É uma questão que varia muito. O Menos é Mais, por exemplo, gastou R$ 11 mil num projeto que deu o retorno que deu, e tem investimento milionário também, pensando em streaming, em página, e que às vezes não teve o sucesso que o 'Churrasquinho' teve."

"Tem uma coisa que é certa na música: o dinheiro não tem retorno certo. Às vezes você investe muito num projeto e o projeto não anda como você esperava e não dá o retorno. Não é sobre o quanto você investe, é sobre você ter uma rotina de investimento que o teu artista suporte o ano inteiro.", explica.

Talvez o gênero que melhor saiba promover suas canções por meio das redes sociais seja o funk.

Queridinho dos influenciadores, o segmento criou todo um ecossistema de promoção envolvendo as plataformas digitais.

Segundo o g1 apurou, essa dinâmica envolve, principalmente, uma estrutura orgânica. Ou seja: MCs insistem para que seus amigos influenciadores postem sua música (geralmente, enviada em primeira mão). Essa troca "na amizade" funciona para funkeiros em destaque.

Agora, se você é um artista iniciante e deseja que sua música vá parar nos stories de um influenciador médio ou em uma página do segmento, vai precisar desembolsar, em média, de R$ 5 mil a R$ 15 mil.

Funcionando num ritmo fabril, a principal empresa do gênero pensou numa estratégia quase óbvia: dominar a produção e a divulgação de ponta a ponta.

É dessa maneira que a GR6, principal produtora de funk do país, barateou seu custo para fazer e promover uma música. Segundo Igor Bittencourt, CEO da empresa, o valor para fazer, lançar e promover uma canção na produtora hoje é de, em média, R$ 70 mil . Da ideia ao lançamento.

Esse modelo orgânico só funciona por conta da produção em níveis cavalares. Na conta de Igor, a GR6 produz cerca de 3 mil músicas por ano. E, ao final do ano, a empresa conta com quase 50 delas que atingiram o top 50 do Spotify — e, sendo assim, deram um bom retorno financeiro.

"Nós trabalhamos no nosso ecossistema, não faz parte do nosso perfil investir, por exemplo, em playlists ou influenciadores. Temos páginas próprias com milhões de seguidores, os próprios perfis dos artistas ajudam. E, na nossa indústria, o que conta é o volume de produção. Temos que errar barato", afirma o executivo.

"Nós lançamos 200 músicas por mês, quase 3.000 por ano. Se 50 dão retorno, o que aconteceu com as outras 2.950 músicas? Custo! E está tudo bem, esse é o negócio, é o business", conclui.

No fim das contas, todos os empresários ouvidos apontam que o investimento financeiro ainda não compra a certeza do sucesso. Mas, com tantos caminhos, o dinheiro se tornou um guia ainda mais certeiro.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' box office collection day 6: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash film earns Rs 823.50 cr worldwide; crosses Rs 400 cr India net
articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive box-office run, with the film crossing the Rs 800 cr worldwide mark within six days
articles.body: Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' continues its impressive box-office run, with the film crossing the Rs 800 cr worldwide mark within six days of its theatrical release. Starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, the mythological epic collected Rs 94.10 cr net in India on Tuesday, November 10. Its domestic gross reached Rs 526.50 cr, while overseas earnings took the worldwide total to Rs 823.50 cr. The film has also crossed the Rs 400 cr India net milestone.Ramayana Movie ReviewThe film registered its latest domestic collection across 24,344 shows. The Hindi version remained the biggest contributor, earning Rs 76.00 cr. Kannada added Rs 7.75 cr, followed by Telugu with Rs 4.00 cr. Tamil and Malayalam contributed Rs 3.60 cr and Rs 2.75 cr, respectively.The overseas market contributed another Rs 35.00 cr on Tuesday. This took the film's cumulative international gross to Rs 297.00 cr. According to Sacnilk, the movie also recorded an average collection of Rs 38,726 per show.'Ramayana' maintains strong box-office momentum despite weekday dipAfter recording a significant jump on Monday, 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' witnessed a 12.5% decline in its India net collection on Tuesday. The film had earned Rs 107.50 cr on its fifth day, making the latest figures a comparatively modest performance. However, its occupancy remained encouraging, indicating continued audience interest during the weekdays.The film opened with Rs 64.85 cr net before experiencing a decline on its second day. Collections recovered over the weekend, followed by another substantial increase on Monday. Its Tuesday performance brought the cumulative India net collection to Rs 440.45 cr. The domestic gross currently stands at Rs 526.50 cr, with 1,42,237 shows recorded across six days.Hindi version contributes the biggest shareThe Hindi version continues to dominate the film's domestic box-office performance. It accounted for 80.8% of the latest day's India net collection. Kannada emerged as the second-largest contributor, while Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam also added to the overall earnings.The cumulative language-wise figures show that Hindi has contributed Rs 336.00 cr, representing 76.3% of the domestic net total. Kannada follows with Rs 41.20 cr, accounting for 9.4%. Telugu has collected Rs 33.00 cr, while Tamil and Malayalam have contributed Rs 17.35 cr and Rs 12.90 cr, respectively.The film's occupancy figures also indicate considerable interest in its regional-language versions. The Kannada 3D release registered 87.70% overall occupancy, while Tamil recorded 84.41%. Hindi stood at 59.42%, and Telugu registered 38.73%. These figures highlight the movie's reach across different markets.'Ramayana' breaks North American first-Monday recordThe film has also achieved a significant milestone in North America. According to Venky Box Office reports, 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' earned approximately USD 1.37 million on its first Monday, surpassing the previous record held by 'Dhurandhar 2'. The achievement makes it the highest first-Monday grosser in the territory.The performance is particularly noteworthy because the movie faced competition from 'Godzilla Minus Zero', which arrived in theatres around the same period. The Japanese franchise's latest instalment reportedly secured considerable premium-screen availability across North America.Venky Box Office reported that 'Ramayana' exceeded the previous first-Monday benchmark of 'Dhurandhar 2' by approximately 20.2%. Its performance also stands out against the opening Monday collections of 'Dangal' and 'Dunki'. Both films benefited from the Christmas holiday period during their respective North American releases.Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi headline the ensemble castDirected by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra, 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend' features Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi in prominent roles. articles.summary: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been returned to federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his court-ordered ankle
articles.body: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been returned to federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his court-ordered ankle monitor. According to latest reports, a federal magistrate judge in Tampa denied him bond on Tuesday, November 10.Prosecutors alleged that Markle had taken off the monitoring device earlier that morning. His arrest follows an FBI investigation into material recovered from storage units registered in his name in Los Angeles.Thomas Markle returns to federal custody after alleged violationAccording to People, Markle was initially arrested last week and released under strict pretrial conditions. These included home detention and electronic location monitoring. However, US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found that he had violated the conditions by allegedly removing his ankle monitor.Markle appeared before the federal magistrate judge in Tampa on Tuesday. The court subsequently revoked his pretrial release and denied him bond. The judge also ordered a medical evaluation, along with continued access to prescribed treatment.FBI seizes 78 items from storage unitsThe investigation began with searches of storage units in Los Angeles that Markle had reportedly rented since 2008. According to the US Department of Justice (DoJ), FBI agents searched the properties under warrants. The most recent payment for the units was reportedly made in October 2026.Investigators seized approximately 78 items during the searches. These included film negatives, photographic slides and books. Authorities allege that the material contained child sexual abuse images.According to the prosecution, witnesses positively identified Markle in two photographs believed to contain such material. Investigators said the man depicted appeared to be between 30 and 40 years old. This suggests that the alleged abuse may date back several decades. Markle is currently reported to be 82.Judge cites housing concerns while ordering medical evaluationAccording to BBC reports, Griffin described Markle's accommodation arrangements as "untenable". In the order revoking his pretrial release, the judge wrote that "based on the lack of suitable housing, no condition or combination of conditions would reasonably assure the safety of any other person or the community and the defendant's appearance in court".The judge also directed that Markle receive a medical assessment. The order stated that he "must receive all necessary and prescribed medication unless discontinued by a physician".Bill Essayli, the US attorney for Central California, also addressed the alleged breach. In a post on X on Tuesday, he wrote: "Release conditions are court orders, not suggestions. We will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law".Thomas Markle denies allegations against himMarkle faces one count of possessing indecent images of children, according to the DoJ (Department of Justice). He has denied possessing child sexual abuse images and described the allegations as "sick lies".The case has also drawn attention to his relationship with Meghan, Duchess of Sussex. The father and daughter have been estranged since 2018. Reportedly Meghan ended contact with him last year. She reportedly told her father that she and the authorities knew about the alleged abuse of young girls.In an earlier statement, Meghan acknowledged receiving a letter concerning the matter. "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," she said. She also explained why she had largely cut off contact with her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".Thomas Markle's career and health backgroundThomas Markle moved to the Philippines last year after suffering a series of strokes. He lived in Cebu until May before returning to Florida. Reports said he was undergoing rehabilitation and learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.Born on July 18, 1944, Thomas Wayne Markle is a retired American television lighting director and director of photography. He received a Chicago/Midwest Emmy Award in 1975 for his work on "Made in Chicago". He also shared two Daytime Emmy Awards for "General Hospital", in 1982 and 2011.Disclaimer: The information in this report is based on a legal hearing as reported by a third-party source. articles.title: Stacy Keach, Star of ‘Mike Hammer,’ ‘Fat City,’ Dies at 85
articles.summary: Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like “Fat City” and the starring role in “The New Mike Hammer” series on CBS, died Tuesday in Pola...
articles.body:
Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like "Fat City" and the starring role in "The New Mike Hammer" series on CBS, died Tuesday in Poland. He was 85.

His wife, Małgosia Tomassi, confirmed his death to Variety . In a statement, she said he died "after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure" at the family's home in Magdalenka, Poland.

"Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family," the statement said. "His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.

Active on stage, film and TV into his eighties, he popped up in "The Bourne Legacy," "Nebraska," "Two and a Half Men," "Ray Donovan" and had a recurring voice role on "The Simpsons." Keach was also known for playing Cardinal Kevin Kearns on "Blue Bloods." His TV appearances included "Man With a Plan" and "The Black List." His final role was in "Jay Kelly" in 2025, as the father of Jay Kelly, played by George Clooney.

In 2010, he received a Helen Hayes award for his performance of "King Lear," for Shakespeare Theater Co., one of many stage honors over the course of his career.

Keach got his Tony nomination for playing Buffalo Bill in the 1969 Broadway production "Indians" early on but garnered even more fame as "Mike Hammer." The CBS series aired from 1984-87 and he reprised the role in the 1989 TV movie "Mike Hammer: Murder Takes All" and the syndicated series "Mike Hammer, Private Eye" in 1997-98.

Keach's run as the private detective got off to a rocky start off screen, however. In 1984, police arrested Keach at London's Heathrow Airport for possession of cocaine. Pleading guilty, the actor served six months at Reading Prison. Since Keach also narrated "Mike Hammer" in character, impressionist Rich Little was called to sub in as the show's narrator during Keach's imprisonment.

In a 2014 television interview, Keach declared that his time in prison was (understandably) the low point of his life, and a friendship he formed with a priest during that time led to his conversion to Roman Catholicism.

Keach's Emmy nomination came shortly after that period; he was recognized in 1988 for outstanding lead actor in a miniseries or special for playing the famous author of the title in "Ernest Hemingway."

Part of an acting family that includes his younger brother James, who has gone on to direct and produce, Walter Stacy Keach Jr. was born in Savannah, Ga., the son of actress Mary Cain and Stacy Keach Sr., an actor, drama teacher and theater director. Class president at Van Nuys High School, he graduated from UC Berkeley in 1963, and went on to earn a graduate degree at the Yale School of Drama. He was also a Fulbright Scholar at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art.

In 1966, Keach played the title role in Barbara Garson's Off Broadway anti-war satire "MacBird!,"winning his first Obie Award. The following year he appeared Off Broadway again, this time with Morgan Freeman (in the latter's acting debut) in George Tabori's provocatively titled "The Niggerlovers."

Keach made his Broadway debut in Georg Buchner's "Danton's Death" in 1965, soon thereafter appearing in a revival of "The Country Wife," followed by the original Broadway production of Bertolt Brecht play "The Caucasian Chalk Circle" and a 1968 staging of "King Lear" in which he played Edmund. The following year he starred in Arthur Kopit's "Indians," picking up his Tony nomination for his performance as Buffalo Bill.

He returned to Broadway in 1979 as a replacement for John Wood as Sidney Bruhl in Ira Levin's long-running mystery comedy "Deathtrap," starred in "Solitary Confinement" in 1992 and in Robert Schenkkan's "The Kentucky Cycle" the following year.

Off Broadway, Keach appeared twice in "Hamlet," in 1964 and 1972, the second time in the title role, winning his second Obie. He also appeared as Falstaff in Henry "IV" Parts I and II in 1968, and as James Tyrone Jr. in O'Neill's "Long Day's Journey Into Night" in 1971.

In the early 1980s he starred in the title role of the national touring company of the Cy Coleman musical "Barnum." He performed the title role in "King Lear" at the Goodman Theater in 2006, and in 2008 played Merlin in a semi-staged version of "Camelot" with the New York Philharmonic.

Keach played Richard M. Nixon in the U.S. traveling version of the play "Frost/Nixon" in 2008 and 2009, in the course of which — one day in March 2009 — he had a series of strokes, from he recovered sufficiently to take another go at "King Lear" in D.C. that summer.

Keach was a founding member of L.A. Theatre Works.

The actor debuted on TV in an episode of college drama "Channing" in 1964, followed by a TV movie versions of Shakespeare's "The Winter's Tale" (1967), in which he played Autolycus, and "Macbeth" (1968), in which he played Banquo. Also in 1968 the actor made his big-screen debut in the adaptation of Carson McCullers' "The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter."

He played a crippled millionaire in Robert Altman's "Brewster McCloud" (1970) and by the next year he starred in the title role of the Western "Doc," playing Doc Holliday opposite Faye Dunaway.

In John Huston's boxing drama "Fat City" (1972), Keach was the over-the-hill boxer praying for a comeback, and Jeff Bridges was the young boxer on the rise.

Also in 1972 the actor starred with George C. Scott and Jane Alexander in the adaptation of Joseph Wambaugh's "The New Centurions" and had a supporting role in Huston's "The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean." He played in a number of roles before stoner comedy classic "Up in Smoke" (1978).

"The Ninth Configuration" (1980), directed by Willliam Peter Blatty and adapted by him from his own surrealist novel "Twinkle Twinkle 'Killer' Kane," became a cult favorite, with Keach's as Marine Col. Vincent Kane who runs a hospital for military men with psychiatric problems.

Also in 1980, the actor appeared with his brother James Keach as Frank and Jesse James in "The Long Riders," and in 1982 he starred with Bruce Dern, Robert Mitchum, Martin Sheen and Paul Sorvino in Jason Miller's "That Championship Season."

Additional film credits include Oliver Stone's biopic "W." (2008), John Sayles' "Honeydripper" (2007) and "Sin City: A Dame to Kill For" (2014). He had a recurring role on "ER" and the Fox comedy "Titus."

H has made numerous guest appearances on shows including "Touched by an Angel," "Will & Grace," "George Lopez," "30 Rock" (as himself), "Anger Management," "Brooklyn Nine-Nine," "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit," "NCIS: New Orleans" and "Hot in Cleveland."

Keach was married four times, first to Kathryn Baker in 1964, then to Marilyn Aiken from 1975-79 and to Jill Donahue from 1981-86.

He is survived by fourth wife Malgosia Tomassi, whom he married in 1986; son Shannon and daughter Karolina and his brother James Keach.

articles.summary: Stacy Keach's wife reveals the lengthy heart failure battle behind the iconic Mike Hammer actor's final days and his extraordinary courage.
articles.body: Stacy Keach, the legendary actor whose unmistakable voice and powerful performances captivated generations of Americans, is being remembered by his beloved wife as a devoted husband, loving father and courageous fighter after his death at 85. Keach, best known for portraying the hard-boiled private detective Mike Hammer and for his celebrated work on stage and screen, died Tuesday, Nov. 10, at his family home in Magdalenka, Poland. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi Keach, shared an emotional statement announcing his passing following a lengthy battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure. PATRICK STEWART, LEGENDARY 'STAR TREK' AND 'X-MEN' ACTOR, DIES AT 86 "It is with profound sadness and a broken heart that I announce the passing of my darling husband, Stacy Keach," she said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital. "After a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, Stacy peacefully departed this world. He fought for so long, with extraordinary courage, determination and strength." She remembered her husband as a man whose remarkable resilience extended far beyond the characters he brought to life on-screen. "He was a true warrior, facing his illness with the same remarkable spirit and resilience that defined his life," she continued. 'TOP GUN' STAR TOM SKERRITT DEAD AT 93 "Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family." For millions of television viewers, Keach will forever be remembered as Mickey Spillane's Mike Hammer, the tough-talking private investigator he portrayed with grit, charisma and an unmistakable screen presence. EVA MARIE SAINT, OSCAR-WINNING ‘ON THE WATERFRONT’ AND ‘NORTH BY NORTHWEST’ STAR, DEAD AT 102 But his extraordinary career stretched far beyond the detective series. A gifted Shakespearean actor, Keach tackled some of theater's most demanding roles, including Hamlet, Richard III and King Lear. He also earned a Golden Globe for his portrayal of Ernest Hemingway. His television appearances included "Blue Bloods," "Titus" and "Prison Break," while his film credits ranged from "The Long Riders" to "Nebraska" and "The Bourne Legacy." Keach also appeared in the Biblical miniseries "Jesus of Nazareth," portraying the criminal Barabbas. In 2017, Keach suffered a heart attack while performing in a one-man production about Ernest Hemingway at Chicago's Goodman Theatre, an ordeal that forced the cancellation of the show's run. Throughout a career spanning more than six decades, Keach earned admiration not only for his versatility but also for the unmistakable voice and commanding presence that made him one of Hollywood's most recognizable performers. Yet for those closest to him, his greatest legacy was the love he shared with his family. "His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives," his wife said. "But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever." His family's farewell was signed with profound love and sorrow by Małgosia, Karolina, Shannon, their grandchildren and spouses.The Associated Press contributed to this reporting.

articles.standfirst: El profesor universitario analiza la polémica en 'La Revuelta'
articles.summary: El profesor universitario analiza la polémica en 'La Revuelta'
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos se ha pronunciado sobre la polémica entrevista de David Broncano, presentador de 'La Revuelta', al candidato de VOX, Santiago Abascal, el pasado lunes. Lejos de sumarse a las críticas, el profesor universitario ha roto una lanza en favor del cómico. "Broncano es un humorista, pero no un periodista y jamás ha ido de lo segundo", ha reflexionado. Gonzalo Bernardos ha señalado que el responsable de este escenario no es el propio David Broncano. "El problema en la entrevista a Abascal es que Moncloa le obligó a convertirse en periodista por un día. Por eso, ha decepcionado a muchas personas. Yo no estoy entre ellas", ha publicado en su cuenta personal de X, antes Twitter. El economista ha ido más allá y ha explicado que la presencia de Santiago Abascal en 'La Revuelta' le ha servido para ver una faceta nueva del presentador: "La entrevista a Abascal me ha permitido conocer el lado humano de Broncano. Y ese lado humano me gusta mucho, pues es poco habitual que en público una estrella de televisión reconozca que lo podía haber hecho mejor. A partir de ahora, lo seguiré más de lo que lo hacía". Gonzalo Bernardos ha felicitado al conductor del programa de La1 por su sinceridad y actitud en los horas posteriores a la polémica entrevista. "Atendió al día siguiente a los medios de comunicación que le pidieron entrevista, explicó cuáles fueron sus errores y por qué no hizo de humorista, que es su principal perfil profesional. Bravo, bravo, bravo". El economista ha lanzado última reflexión en sus redes sociales: "¿Por qué quiso TVE (Moncloa) que Broncano entrevistara a Abascal? Porque pretendía q la entrevista tuviera la máxima audiencia posible. Dos propósitos posibles: Abascal se pusiera nervioso e hiciera el ridículo; potenciar la imagen de Abascal. ¿Cuál creéis que es el verdadero?".

articles.title: Roma’s Title Push Faces Bigger Tests
articles.summary: Roma have entered the November international break just two points off the top of Serie A. Saturday’s 3-0 win over Sassuolo took Gian Piero Gasperini’s side...
articles.body:
Roma have entered the November international break just two points off the top of Serie A. Saturday's 3-0 win over Sassuolo took Gian Piero Gasperini's side to 27 points from 11 matches, behind Lazio on 29 and Inter on 28. Unbeaten in the league with 31 goals, Roma have established themselves among the contenders. Staying there will be harder.

Sassuolo arrived at the Olimpico with four straight league defeats, but Roma still had to break down a crowded defence. Mario Hermoso opened the scoring, Sebastian Walukiewicz turned a Donyell Malen effort into his own net, and Rodrigo Mora added the third. Roma finished with 28 shots.

Malen remains a threat through the middle, Matias Soulé creates openings in tight spaces, and Mora has given Gasperini another attacking option. The coach singled out the variety of Roma's goals after Saturday's win.

That variety will matter against teams able to put Roma under pressure. A comfortable home win tells us less about how they will handle a difficult away fixture.

Two points is a small gap in November, but it says little about how Roma, Inter or Lazio will perform over the remaining months. Title odds account for future fixtures, squad strength and injuries rather than simply repeating the standings.

Bookmakers set odds, including a margin, and adjust them as conditions change. That differs from how Kalshi prediction markets work , where traders buy and sell contracts tied to defined outcomes. A contract priced at 30 cents may suggest a roughly 30% market-implied chance, but it is no guarantee and doesn't imply a Roma-specific contract exists.

A forecast may move while Roma aren't playing because of news about a rival, an injury or trading activity. That is different from a change in Roma's league position.

Gasperini still considers Inter the leading title contenders , despite Roma's form. Asked after the Sassuolo match whether he would settle for second place, he said no. He recognises the opportunity without treating the race as settled.

Roma's Champions League defeats to Real Madrid and Manchester United show what remains to be fixed. They led by two goals in both matches before losing. Those results don't erase an unbeaten league start, but they raise questions about how Roma respond when momentum turns.

They will need greater control against domestic rivals, particularly when three goals aren't forthcoming.

Roma visit Parma on 21 November. Gasperini recently highlighted a run of nine matches in 27 days, including both European defeats. The international break offers some respite, though several players will be away with their national teams.

Paulo Dybala and Mile Svilar have missed recent games. Roma's ability to rotate without losing their attacking threat may prove as important as the quality of their first-choice eleven. The coming fixtures will test that depth.

Any odds comparison needs a date and a clearly defined outcome. Roma's chances of winning at Parma aren't the same as their chances of winning Serie A, and pre-season prices are already outdated.

Prediction-market prices also come with limitations. The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission covers contract rules, fees and potential losses in its guidance on event contracts . Thin trading may make a price less informative than it looks; no single figure provides a precise measure of Roma's prospects.

For Roma supporters, a change in the numbers only means something when its cause is clear: a result, an injury or a tougher assessment of the fixture list.

With 27 points and 31 goals after 11 matches, Roma belong in the Scudetto conversation. Their attack has earned that attention, while the European defeats show why Gasperini still has work to do. The coming weeks will reveal whether Roma can sustain this pace against stronger opponents and a demanding schedule. Their next results, rather than a shift in the odds, will show how much of that early promise can last.

articles.title: Country star Craig Morgan says he's 'willing to die' for America after returning to military service
articles.summary: Craig Morgan says he's willing to die for America's freedoms as the U.S. Army reserve officer releases his patriotic new album "My Country."
articles.body: Country singer Craig Morgan, a U.S. Army Reserve warrant officer, says he is willing to die for his country to preserve America's freedoms. "I am willing to go wherever they send me and do whatever it takes to ensure that we maintain the freedoms," Morgan, who reenlisted in the Army in 2023 after previously serving for nearly two decades, told Fox News Digital. "And not for me, but for my family, for my friends, for my friend's kids, and for the kids that I don't even know." He said he thinks every American service member feels the same way he does. AARON TIPPIN SAYS PATRIOTISM IS 'VERY STRONG IN AMERICA' AHEAD OF FORT CAMPBELL 4TH OF JULY SHOW "Listen, like the [Toby Keith] song ‘American Soldier’ says, ‘I don't want to die, but if dying is asked of me, I will.’ And I believe that more people, even those that don't serve, feel that way." The "Redneck Yacht Club" singer, who lives in Tennessee, said, "That's what we celebrate." LEE GREENWOOD SAYS HE'S 'VERY PROUD' TO STAND NEXT TO TRUMP DURING AMERICA'S 250TH CELEBRATION "But absolutely, I am willing to die for my country and to die for the freedoms that I get to celebrate. I want my grandchildren and their children and their grandchildren to celebrate those same freedoms." Morgan released a new 11-song album, "My Country," on Nov. 6, which features a cover of "American Soldier." CARRIE UNDERWOOD, GARY SINISE LEAD STARS WHO'VE SHARED WHY THEY'RE PROUD TO BE AMERICANS "We're celebrating our 250th," he said. "I just felt like it was most appropriate as we celebrate that as a nation that I'm able to do it in my genre, in my format, in my occupation." WATCH: CRAIG MORGAN SAYS HE IS WILLING TO DIE FOR HIS COUNTRY He said he feels like he’s always celebrating America, "but we took it, I feel like we took it a step further with this actual project, a physical project, celebrating our nation, hence the name ‘My Country,’ but for me, it had a dual implication." COUNTRY STAR CHRIS JANSON SAYS RESPECTING THE FLAG IS THE NUMBER ONE LESSON HE WANTS HIS KIDS TO LEARN At the risk of sounding biased, Morgan said he thinks country music "celebrates the love and passion for our freedom and for our nation much more than the other genres." KID ROCK TAPS EMINEM FOR CHRISTIAN ALBUM, PLANS BEER-AND-FAITH ARENA REVIVALS "We don't shy away or steer away from our belief in God, family, and country," he added, "and this project really kind of hits at both of those, both of my worlds, my military world and my music world." The 62-year-old is especially proud of the original track "Long May You Wave," which he called "extremely personal" and emotional. BLACK RIFLE COFFEE CO-FOUNDER RELEASES NEW MUSIC VIDEO HONORING FALLEN SOLDIERS AHEAD OF MEMORIAL DAY "Having served in the military for over 20 years now, that flag represents something that I think — there was a time in our nation that it had been taken for granted. I do believe that we're back in a place where we respect that flag, we respect what it stands for. And I'm not saying that we didn't, but I think generally we lost sight of what it is that flag represented and the many, many men and women who have sacrificed in order to ensure that that representation is not tarnished." The song is about middle-class America — "the people that really built this country and the people whose backs we stand on," he said. DOLLY PARTON'S ‘ALL-AMERICAN HEART’: HOW COUNTRY ICON FORGED SPECIAL BOND WITH US MILITARY The cover of "American Soldier" is in honor of Keith "and in honor of what he stood for," he explained. "For me, that song again is extremely personal," he said. "I am an American soldier and I love my country and I love what this song says about us." Morgan said service members don’t "stand out there and wave our flag, so to speak, but this song is a testament to, in my opinion, the moral fiber that makes up those people who serve our nation. And I'm grateful to have the honor to be able to record that song." WATCH: CRAIG MORGAN ON WHY HE'S RELEASING HIS PATRIOTIC ‘MY COUNTRY’ ALBUM NOW He added that country music offers listeners a "sense of reality, a sense of truth. Also, all of this wrapped up in humility, grace, and gratitude." "The general populace of the country music format, including the artists, come from a place of humble beginnings, come from a place of Middle America," he said. "We talk about, sing about, and represent, and live the lifestyle of the people that build America, as I alluded to earlier. And I still live that lifestyle. A lot of people don't believe it. I mean, you know, I don't always cut my own grass, but I do sometimes, but I still take off my own garbage when I'm home." Speaking about his own family, Morgan said he hopes his grandchildren "inherit the attitude towards our nation that my grandfather had and that I feel like I have."
