articles.title: Kylie Jenner’s ex-housekeeper says she was locked in closet, bit by dog and pepper sprayed working for mogul
articles.summary: Kylie Jenner’s former housekeeper is suing the reality star and cosmetics mogul, alleging that she was trapped inside Jenner’s closet, bitten by a dog and accidentally pepper sprayed in the face.
articles.body: Kylie Jenner’s former housekeeper is suing the reality star and cosmetics mogul, alleging that she was trapped inside Jenner’s closet, bitten by a dog and accidentally pepper sprayed in the face. The new lawsuit marks the fourth time the 29-year-old co-star of “The Kardashians” and founder of Kylie Cosmetics has been sued by members of her household staff within the last seven months. Dinora Carolina Cabria Amaya filed the lawsuit in Los Angeles Superior Court on Nov. 5, accusing Jenner, her company and two members of her staff — Laura Dooley and Itzel Sibrian — of disability discrimination, retaliation, wrongful termination and numerous labor violations. Amaya worked at several of Jenner’s California residences from March 2025 until she was fired in February 2026, according to the complaint. She earned $40 an hour — roughly $23 above the state’s minimum wage — and worked six days a week. Jenner owns several multimillion-dollar properties in the Los Angeles metropolitan area, in addition to a La Quinta mansion outside of Palm Springs. The former housekeeper alleges that on an unspecified date she became locked inside Jenner’s closet and “confined against her will.” The complaint states that Dooley instructed her to enter the closet and gave her the passcode, but that Amaya became locked inside. When she became trapped, Amaya called Dooley, who “laughed and mocked her,” and “refused to disclose the access information necessary to obtain her release,” according to the lawsuit. Amaya alleged she had a panic attack and was trapped inside the closet for more than an hour. On Sept. 4, 2025, while cleaning and organizing a drawer in one of Jenner’s laundry rooms, an unsecured canister of pepper spray discharged directly into Amaya’s eyes and face, the lawsuit alleges. The more Amaya “complained that she was hurt, the harder Defendants made her job,” removing other staffers who had been helping Amaya and requiring her to complete work alone, according to the complaint. On Oct. 28, 2025, Amaya was assigned to clean a doghouse, according to the complaint. While performing the assigned work, a dog bit her, according to the suit. The lawsuit does not state who the dog belonged to. Jenner has owned several dogs since she was a teenager, with some of them being prominently featured on her family’s former reality show “Keeping Up With The Kardashians.” Amaya alleged that after she complained about her injuries, Jenner’s staff “increased her workload, assigned heavier tasks, and abruptly changed her schedule and work locations.” “Defendants were making her life miserable so she would quit,” the lawsuit states. Michael Rhodes, a lawyer for Jenner, noted in a statement to NBC News that the four cases brought against his client were being represented by the same attorney. “It’s clear that this lawyer wants to use publicity to try and extract an unwarranted payday. We’re not going to be intimidated into doing that,” Rhodes said. “As such, we’ll defend these meritless cases vigorously and look forward to telling our side of the story.” When asked about Rhodes’ comments, Della Shaker, the lawyer representing all four of the people suing Jenner, said in a statement her goal was “to litigate the facts, not trade insults.” “We came prepared with evidence, not publicity stunts,” she said. “Attempts to intimidate and silence my clients may have worked before they had someone willing to stand up for them. Those days are over.” Sibrian declined to comment. A woman who answered a phone number associated with Dooley hung when asked about her employment. Jenner was first sued by former members of her staff in April, when another former housekeeper, Angelica Hernandez Vasquez, alleged she was discriminated against. Vasquez alleged that she was “mocked for accent and treated as inferior because of her Salvadoran background” and discriminated against for being Catholic. Vasquez additionally accused one of her supervisors of throwing a clothing hanger at Vasquez’s feet while reprimanding her. Later that month, Juana Delgado Soto sued Jenner alleging that she endured years of discrimination, humiliation and wage violations while working as a housekeeper for Jenner for more than six years. And in June, a private chef who worked for Jenner alleged that she suffered a miscarriage in February 2025 while working for Jenner. The chef, who is only identified as Jane Doe, was under “overwhelming physical strain” while working at a birthday party for Jenner’s child’s in Palm Springs on February 1, 2025, according to the lawsuit. Her “requests for assistance were dismissed” and met with “hostility,” the lawsuit alleges. The next day, the chef woke up to severe hemorrhaging and lost her unborn child, the lawsuit states. She was five months pregnant. The chef alleged that she was fired in late March, weeks after returning from medical leave for the miscarriage.

articles.title: Muere Stacy Keach, el actor que interpretó al detective Mike Hammer y ganó un Globo de Oro por dar vida a Ernest Hemingway
articles.standfirst: El intérprete estadounidense ha fallecido este martes en su residencia de Polonia, tras sufrir una grave enfermedad cardíaca
articles.summary: El intérprete estadounidense ha fallecido este martes en su residencia de Polonia, tras sufrir una grave enfermedad cardíaca
articles.body: El actor estadounidense Stacy Keach ha fallecido este martes a los 85 años de edad en su domicilio familiar de Magdalenka, en Polonia, donde residía junto a su familia. Conocido internacionalmente por interpretar al detective privado Mike Hammer en la televisión, el intérprete deja tras de sí una trayectoria de más de seis décadas en el cine, el teatro y la pequeña pantalla. La noticia ha sido confirmada por su esposa, la actriz y antigua modelo polaca Małgosia Tomassi, quien ha explicado que el actor padecía desde hacía tiempo una grave afección cardíaca que terminó provocándole una insuficiencia cardíaca. "Después de una larga y difícil batalla contra una grave afección cardíaca e insuficiencia cardíaca, Stacy abandonó este mundo en paz", ha comunicado su mujer, según declaraciones recogidas por la revista People. En el mismo mensaje, ha querido recordar tanto su dimensión profesional como personal: "Stacy no solo fue un actor legendario, admirado y querido por el público de todo el mundo, sino también mi amado esposo, mi compañero y el corazón de nuestra familia". Stacy Keach falleció rodeado de sus seres queridos. Nacido en una familia vinculada al mundo de la interpretación, era hijo del actor, productor y director Stacy Keach Sr. y de la actriz Mary Cain, el intérprete descubrió desde muy joven su vocación artística. Estudió Literatura Inglesa y Arte Dramático en la Universidad de California en Berkeley y posteriormente amplió su formación en la prestigiosa Escuela de Arte Dramático de Yale. También obtuvo una beca Fulbright para estudiar en la London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art, en Reino Unido. Antes de alcanzar la popularidad televisiva, Stacy Keach desarrolló una sólida carrera teatral. Dio vida a personajes de William Shakespeare como Hamlet y Enrique V y consiguió una nominación al premio Tony en 1969 por su interpretación de Buffalo Bill en la obra 'Indians'. Su gran reconocimiento popular llegó en 1983, cuando protagonizó la película para televisión 'Murder Me, Murder You' y se metió por primera vez en la piel de Mike Hammer, el detective privado creado por el escritor Mickey Spillane. El personaje regresó en la serie 'The New Mike Hammer', emitida entre 1984 y 1987, y posteriormente en 'Mike Hammer, Private Eye', entre 1997 y 1998. Aunque Mike Hammer fue el papel que más contribuyó a su popularidad, Stacy Keach demostró su versatilidad en numerosos proyectos cinematográficos y televisivos. Uno de sus trabajos más destacados llegó en 1988 con la miniserie 'Hemingway', en la que interpretó al célebre escritor estadounidense Ernest Hemingway. Para preparar el personaje, el actor llegó a ganar alrededor de 16 kilos, en una transformación física que acompañó a una interpretación reconocida con el Globo de Oro al mejor actor en una miniserie o película para televisión. También obtuvo una candidatura al premio Emmy por este trabajo. En la gran pantalla participó en películas como 'Fat City', 'The Long Riders', 'The Ninth Configuration', 'Up in Smoke', 'Escape from L.A.', 'American History X' y 'Nebraska', entre otras. Una filmografía que refleja una carrera especialmente extensa y alejada de un único registro interpretativo. En el terreno personal, Stacy Keach estuvo casado en cuatro ocasiones. Su última esposa fue Małgosia Tomassi, a quien conoció durante el rodaje de la serie Mike Hammer. Su relación se prolongó durante 40 años y juntos tuvieron dos hijos, Shannon y Karolina. La familia residía en Polonia, país en el que el actor obtuvo la ciudadanía en 2015 y donde ha fallecido a los 85 años.

articles.title: Admins intensifies preparations for Chhath festival
articles.summary: Prayagraj ramps up Chhath Puja preparations for Nov 13-16, focusing on ghat safety, crowd/traffic control, cleaning, lighting and amenities at Sangam.
articles.body: Prayagraj: Elaborate preparations have been made for Chhath festival to be observed from Nov 13 to 16 in Sangam city.The festival will begin with Nahay Khay on Friday (Nov 13) followed by Kharna, Sandhya Arghya, Usha Arghya and Paran. In view of the upcoming four-day festival, the district administration has intensified preparations to ensure the convenience and safety of devotees at Sangam and Yamuna river banks (ghats).Senior police and administrative officials have focused on crowd and traffic management at ghats and even conducted an on-site inspection at the ghats to review the existing arrangements. Officials also issued directives to ensure that tasks including the levelling and cleaning of ghats, removal of silt, repair of damaged roads, potable water, traffic parking, and the installation of lighting were completed within the stipulated time frame.In the city, local markets have transformed into bustling hubs decked with traditional offerings, seasonal produce, and handcrafted bamboo goods for the four-day Chhath Puja festival.Noted religious scholar Dr Amitabh Gour said, “On Friday (first Day of festival) will be observed Nahay-Khay where devotees after bathing, particularly those observing the fast, will consume a pure, sattvic meal (like arwa rice, bottle gourd curry, and split Bengal gram or chana dal). On second Day (November 14) will be observed Kharna and devotees will observe fast without water (nirjala) for the entire day. In the evening, they will break their fast (paran) by consuming rasiyav (kheer made with jaggery) and roti as prasad.”The third day (November 15) will be observed as Sandhya Arghya. On this day, devotees will visit the banks of a river or pond to offer arghya (oblations) to the setting sun. On this night, the traditions of Kosi Bharai and deepotsav are to be observed.On the fourth day (Nov 16), devotees will observe Usha Arghya and Paran. In the early morning, arghya (Usha Arghya) is offered to the rising sun. Following this, the observers consume prasad to conclude the fast (paran).Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news.
